Recruiter scope returns leads_added_today=17 and can_filter_recruiter=false; team_leader=22. Admin recruiter_id filter narrows to owner. Fresh Leads => /api/leads?status=new returns 8 items. (b) My Day recruiter counts match spec exactly {overdue:2, today:3, never_called:5, high_priority:2, iv_conf:2, join_conf:1, tasks:2}; completing a today followup decrements the count on next fetch (live). (c) Quick actions: POST /leads and POST /tasks persist and appear in list. Direct URL /admin/settings, /admin/audit-logs, /admin/recruiters all render 'Access denied — You do not have permission to view this section.' My Day page renders with 7 myday-step-* keys and progress %. Notification bell shows unread count derived from user's overdue/today follow-ups + interviews.
critical_code_review_comments: services/dashboard_service.py: recruiter_id filter in compute() maps any non-scope id to ['__none__'] and shows 0 KPIs. That's correct denial behaviour, but the API returns 200 rather than 403; recommend documenting so clients don't confuse 'no data' with 'valid empty result'.

services/myday_service.py: progress_percent uses steps_complete / total_steps, but a step is 'complete' only when count==0. Progress therefore reports 0% for a recruiter who still has any pending item in ANY of the 7 lists — even if 6 lists are already clear (e.g. Jordan currently 0%). Consider weighting by remaining items or reporting per-step completion for a smoother UX.

api/recruitment_routes.py::list_leads: response shape swings between list and {items:...}. Frontend already tolerates both, but consider always returning {items, total, page, page_size} for consistency and paging correctness.

api/dashboard_routes.py::overview: parse_range default (no query params) uses org timezone 'today' — good. However, dashboard aggregates like 'calls_today' and 'leads_added_today' both use the same rng; explicit test verifies exact seeded counts so any tz drift is caught here. Keep the seed_service tied to the same tz to avoid future flakiness.

services/user_service.set_active: revokes sessions on deactivation (good) but does not revoke sessions on role change; consider revoking on role change so cached permission scopes cannot outlive the change. Not blocking.
role_routes.update_role blocks 'admin' with 400 (good). But there is no similar block on delete_role for role_key == 'admin' if is_system was accidentally false — extra defensive check recommended.
